answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by requiring each new identity to lock a refundable bond, moved in over a bridge from an external chain and held in escrow. Like cargo inspected at a wharf before it can cross a river, the bond stays frozen through a probationary window while peers check the agent work; linked fake accounts showing coordinated fraud lose the whole bond. Honest agents recover it, but an attacker spinning up thousands of identities must lock real capital for every one, making the swarm cost more than it can earn.
